subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Printing Press: Engineering Mass Communication
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Printing Press: Engineering Mass Communication.

hook.text: Before Gutenberg, a single book took months to copy by hand. A Bible cost a year's salary.

buildup.text: Gutenberg combined a wine press, movable metal type, and oil-based ink into one machine.

discovery.text: His press could produce 3,600 pages per day. A monk could copy about 4. That's a 900x improvement.

twist.text: Gutenberg went bankrupt. His investor seized the press and the profits from the famous Bible.

climax.text: Within 50 years, 20 million books existed in Europe. Knowledge was no longer controlled by the few.

punchline.text: One machine ended the monopoly on knowledge.

quiz.question: How much faster was Gutenberg's press compared to hand-copying?
